title: Rectangular prism
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety, zero, and negative ninety degrees, and the translation vector to zero, zero, and zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch of a single face. Construct a closed loop with four lines: the first line starts at the origin and ends at zero point zero four eight three, zero; the second line starts at zero point zero four eight three, zero and ends at zero point zero four eight three, zero point zero zero zero five; the third line starts at zero point zero four eight three, zero point zero zero zero five and ends at zero, zero point zero zero zero five; the fourth line starts at zero, zero point zero zero zero five and returns to the origin. Scale the two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point zero four eight three. Rotate the scaled two-dimensional sketch using the Euler angles set in the coordinate system, and translate it using the translation vector. Extrude the transformed two-dimensional sketch along the normal direction by zero point seven five units, ensuring that this operation creates a new solid body. The resulting rectangular prism has a length of zero point zero four eight two six seven five nine two two three zero nine eight zero three six units, a width of zero point zero zero zero four nine five zero five two two two eight zero one zero zero five four three units, and a height of zero point seven five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0483, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0483, 0.0005) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0005) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r  # This will represent the final model

import cadquery as cq

# Dimensions
L = 0.7500  # length along X
W = 0.0483  # width along Y
T = 0.0005  # thickness along Z

# Create a thin flat rectangular strip
r = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .box(L, W, T, centered=(True, True, True))
)
